name: Hotel Delmano
take: Marble bar, cracked mirrors, and cocktails built slowly under low light; the Williamsburg bar for a date that is already going well.
theCatch: No standing and no reservations, so a Friday table means arriving before 8 or waiting outside.
notes: Corner of Berry and N 9th. Open 4pm-1am Mon-Thu, 4pm-2am Fri, 2pm-2am Sat, 2pm-1am Sun. Seasonal cocktails, a wine list of around 100 bottles from small producers, and a raw bar with oysters, ceviche, tartare, cheese and charcuterie. Seated-only policy; no reservations listed on the site.

name: Fresh Kills Bar
take: A small, serious cocktail room on Grand Street where the bartenders ask what you like and hand you something better.
theCatch: Happy hour is 5 to 7 with $10 cocktails; the leather booths are gone by 9 on weekends.
notes: Between Bedford and Berry on Grand. Milk & Honey lineage: hand-cut ice, house syrups, fresh juice, classics plus low-ABV options. Daily happy hour 5-7pm with $10 cocktails; regular cocktails mid-teens and up. Small room with booths and exposed brick, snacks only; weekend nights bring a line.

name: Deux Chats
take: Martinis, dollar oysters at happy hour, and a vaulted, mirrored room under the bridge that makes a Tuesday feel like an occasion.
theCatch: Oysters are $1 until 6pm; after that cocktails run $17-21 and a table wants a Resy.
notes: South Williamsburg, Broadway between Kent and Wythe, from the Le Dive / The Nines team; opened 2022. Hours Mon-Wed 5pm-12am, Thu 5pm-1am, Fri 2pm-2am, Sat 3pm-2am, Sun 3-11pm. Happy hour until 6pm: $1 oysters, $13 house martini, beer-and-shot. Belle Epoque room with distressed mirrors and cat murals; crudo, sardines, seafood plateaus. Walk-ins fine, Resy for tables.

name: Layla
take: A cocktail bar with a big leafy backyard that fills with couples on weeknights; bring someone you want to sit across from.
theCatch: Weekday happy hour 4 to 6 has $12 negronis and martinis; the backyard goes first when it is warm.
notes: Bedford Ave south of Grand, between S 3rd and S 4th. Cocktails plus a snack menu (oysters, small plates) and a large backyard that reads as a date garden on weeknights. Happy hour Mon-Fri 4-6pm: $12 negronis, martinis and spritzes, $6 drafts, $2 oysters.

name: Sauced
take: No menu and no attitude: tell the bartender what you are into and drink whatever natural wine they pour next.
theCatch: Food is whatever pop-up is in that week, so eat first; check the patio under the tree before settling inside.
notes: Natural-wine-only bar on Bedford between S 3rd and S 4th, no printed list; staff pour tastes until you land on a glass. French, Spanish and Italian producers, from single glasses to older bottles. Hours Mon-Thu 5pm-12am, Fri 5pm-2am, Sat 3pm-2am, Sun 3pm-12am. Small plates were dropped in favor of rotating pop-ups. Second location opened in Manhattan in 2024.

name: Rocka Rolla
take: Classic rock on the stereo, beer in goblets, a pool table, and a 4am close; the dive you end up at, on purpose.
theCatch: Order the big goblet, claim the backyard shuffleboard, and expect the room to double after midnight on weekends.
notes: Corner bar on Metropolitan between Rodney and Union, a block from the Lorimer L / Metropolitan G. Cheap domestic beer served in schooners and large chalices, retro rock decor, pool table inside; backyard has shuffleboard and pinball. Open until 4am. Cards accepted. Tripadvisor listed it as open in 2026.

name: The Levee
take: A Berry Street dive open till 4 with free cheese balls, chili dogs, and no interest in impressing anybody.
theCatch: Nearly always full at night; the back patio and the pool table are the two things worth angling for.
notes: Corner of Berry and N 3rd, next door to Radegast and catches its overflow. Open daily noon-4am since 2005. Free cheese balls at the bar, chili dogs and Frito pie from the kitchen, cheap beer-and-shot deals, pool table, darts, jukebox, Big Buck Hunter, and a back patio where dogs show up. Happy hour 5-8pm is $1 off everything.

name: Pete's Candy Store
take: A narrow bar with a tiny train-car stage in back, free shows every night, and a backyard that keeps the Lorimer crowd around.
theCatch: Happy hour is $6 drinks until 7 on weekdays; the back room is small, so get in before the set starts.
notes: Former 1920s candy shop on Lorimer between Frost and Richardson, open since 1999. Free live shows nightly with no cover in a narrow, Pullman-car-shaped back room; also weekly trivia, bingo and open mics. Hours roughly 4-5pm to 2am weekdays, 3pm-2am weekends; happy hour Mon-Fri until 7pm with $6 drafts, wells and wine. Food is grilled cheese and chips. Seasonal garden patio.

name: Night of Joy
take: Two floors of antiques, cheap-enough cocktails, and a rooftop deck strung with lights; the first-date bar for people still deciding.
theCatch: The rooftop runs weekends only; happy hour is 5 to 8 daily, and downstairs is calmer on a weeknight.
notes: Lorimer at Jackson, a few blocks north of the Lorimer L. Bi-level bar with old couches and Victorian odds and ends downstairs and a second-story roof patio with string lights and trellised plants; per Time Out the upstairs bar opens weekends only. Cocktails lean on herbal infusions; also frozen margaritas. Happy hour daily 5-8pm.

name: Metropolitan
take: Brooklyn's original queer dive: cheap beer, a backyard, a small dance floor, and a crowd that talks to strangers.
theCatch: Summer Sunday backyard barbecues and Tuesday Queeraoke are the nights; the rest of the week it is a proper neighborhood bar.
notes: Lorimer just south of Metropolitan Ave, across from Bagelsmith; open since 2002 and still the anchor of Williamsburg's queer scene. Multi-level room with pool table, small dance floor and a backyard patio. Sunday barbecues Memorial Day through September, Queeraoke Tuesdays, Wednesday trivia, monthly drag and comedy nights. Cheap beer-and-shot specials.

name: Lucky Dog
take: A Bedford Avenue beer bar where the backyard doubles as an off-leash dog run and nobody has ever dressed up.
theCatch: Twenty taps and big pours around $10; the courtyard is the whole point, so pick a dry night.
notes: Bedford between S 1st and S 2nd, marked by a cartoon dog on the storefront. Around 20 taps heavy on Allagash and Ommegang plus a full bar, jukebox of classic rock and country, shuffleboard, and a brick courtyard where dogs run off-leash. Time Out lists noon-4am daily. Tripadvisor showed it open in 2026.

name: The Quarter Club
take: A projector, a wall of TVs, pinball machines, and wings that come out of the kitchen all night; the Grand Street sports bar for a pregame.
theCatch: Loud and overstimulating by design; grab a table before kickoff and do not skip the wings.
notes: Grand between Havemeyer and Marcy. Giant projector plus multiple TVs, pinball machines (Foo Fighters, Demolition Man, Hot Wheels), and a kitchen doing buttermilk-brined wings, chicken sandwiches and burgers. Beers from around $6. Infatuation review updated July 2025.

name: Berry Park
take: Two levels, fifteen European taps, a soccer screen the size of a wall, and a rooftop a block from McCarren Park; where big groups go.
theCatch: Closed Mondays; match days and the weekend rooftop DJ fill it fast, so send someone up early.
notes: Berry at N 14th, one block west of McCarren Park on the Williamsburg/Greenpoint line; women-owned, open since 2009. Roughly 3,500 sq ft beer hall downstairs with about 15 German/Belgian taps, communal tables and a 13-foot soccer screen; rooftop nearly as big with skyline views and no-cover DJs on weekends. Burgers, mac and cheese, fish and chips; weekend brunch. Recent hours: closed Mon, Tue-Thu 4pm-12am, Fri 3pm-2am, Sat 11am-2am, Sun 11am-12am.

name: St. Mazie
take: Live jazz every night, oysters at the bar, and a garden out back; the Grand Street room for a date that needs a soundtrack.
theCatch: Happy hour 5 to 7 has $2 oysters; the cellar supper club takes bookings, the front bar mostly does not need one.
notes: Grand between Havemeyer and Marcy. Jazz bar and restaurant open seven nights (Mon-Thu from 6pm, Fri-Sun from 5pm) with live music nightly, swing and gypsy jazz in the main room and a Cellar Supper Club downstairs; garden in back. Raw bar and American menu; happy hour 5-7pm with $5 beer, $6 wine, $2 oysters. Reservations on Resy; hosts buyouts and private events. Tripadvisor listed it as open in 2026.

name: Desert 5 Spot
take: A hangar-sized honky-tonk with a mechanical bull, a band, and ranch water; the bachelorette bar you go to on purpose, with the right group.
theCatch: Weekend lines and boots-optional crowds; bring a group and a sense of humor, not a first date.
notes: Wythe at N 11th, across from the Wythe Hotel; an LA import that opened in Williamsburg in 2024. Huge Western-themed room with a live stage, mechanical bull, hay bales, wagon-wheel chandeliers, a Dolly Parton photo wall and a cowboy-boot disco ball. Ranch waters and tacos. Draws bachelorette parties and big groups; line dancing happens.

name: Bembe
take: A candlelit room under the bridge where DJs and live drummers keep people dancing to salsa, reggae, and cumbia until 4.
theCatch: Cash only, opens late, and does not get going before midnight; the room is small, so arrive before the line.
notes: Unmarked doorway at S 6th and Berry, under the Williamsburg Bridge near the Marcy J/M/Z; running since the early 2000s. Nightly DJs spinning Afro-Latin, reggae, salsa, cumbia and funk, often with live percussion over the mix. Time Out has listed it as opening around 8:30pm and closing 4am; cash only. Own site lists the address but no hours; verify before sending a group.

name: Baby's All Right
take: Part bar, part venue: catch a band in the back room, then stay for the crowd that spills out to the front bar after.
theCatch: Shows are ticketed and sell out; the front bar and restaurant take walk-ins, so you can still drink there without a ticket.
notes: Broadway at Bedford, near the Marcy J/M/Z; opened 2013. About 5,000 sq ft: a front bar and eatery (Latin-leaning dinner, small plates, weekend brunch) plus a 330-capacity standing room booking indie, rock, jazz, electronic and experimental acts nightly. Co-founder Billy Jones died in June 2025; the venue continues under partner Zachary Mexico and opened a sister room, Night Club 101, in the East Village in 2025.

name: St. Anselm
take: A tiny grill-and-counter steakhouse where the butcher's steak is still the order and nobody needs a jacket.
theCatch: Walk-ins are first come, first served; after 7 on a weekend the wait is real, so aim for the counter.
notes: Across Metropolitan from The Commodore, near the Lorimer L. Open 5-11pm Mon-Fri; Sat-Sun lunch 12-4 and dinner 5-11. Narrow room with roughly eight tables plus counter seats at the open grill; butcher's steak around $29, big-format ax-handle rib eye by the ounce. Walk-ins first come, first served with Resy also available. Bedford-side neighbor Spuyten Duyvil is the classic waiting spot.

name: Fish Cheeks Williamsburg
take: Family-style Thai seafood with heat and sour in equal measure; the Driggs Avenue dinner that sets up a night out around the corner.
theCatch: Oyster happy hour runs noon to 6 daily; the back room is quieter, and the kitchen stops a little after 10.
notes: Driggs between N 8th and N 9th, a short walk from the Bedford L. Brooklyn outpost of the NoHo Thai seafood spot: bright curries, whole fish, oysters. Open Sun-Thu 12-10:15pm, Fri-Sat 12-10:45pm; oyster happy hour daily 12-6pm. Communal-style seating with a more casual back room; reservations online.

name: Birds of a Feather
take: Sichuan for a table of six: chili wontons, dan dan noodles, and a bright room that turns tables fast enough to keep the night moving.
theCatch: Book on Resy or expect a wait; last seating is 9:30 most nights and 10 on Friday and Saturday.
notes: Grand between Bedford and Driggs. Sichuan restaurant from the Cafe China team with a big communal table up front and a small bar. Dinner Sun-Thu 4:30-10pm (last seating 9:30), Fri-Sat 4:30-10:30pm (last seating 10); lunch daily. Portions are large and most dishes sit under or around $20 with gratuity built in; poached chili wontons and Chungking chicken are the calls. Resy.

name: Laser Wolf
take: Israeli skewers over charcoal on the Hoxton roof, with the skyline and a spread of salads included; dinner that already feels like the night out.
theCatch: Dinner is on Resy; the ten-seat bar is first come, and the sunset seats are the ones everyone wants.
notes: Rooftop of the Hoxton, Wythe at N 10th. Philadelphia-born shipudiya from the Zahav team: charcoal-grilled skewers with a set of salatim included, Israeli snacks and Middle Eastern-leaning cocktails, uninterrupted Manhattan views. Dinner reservations on Resy; a 10-seat bar is first come, first served.

name: Kellogg's Diner
take: A 24-hour diner with a full bar and a Tex-Mex streak; the after-bar meal that also works as the first stop of the night.
theCatch: Late night it turns into a scene with music on; brunch is families, so pick your hour accordingly.
notes: Corner of Metropolitan and Union at the Lorimer L / Metropolitan G. Landmark diner (seen in HBO's Girls) that closed in 2023 and reopened in 2024 under the team behind Old John's, with chrome trim, pink-beige booths, a full cocktail bar and a Tex-Mex-inflected menu: guajillo short rib hash, honey-butter chicken biscuit, ribs, flat nachos. Open 24 hours; Resy available. Infatuation review updated June 2026.
